readme.html:
blueprint

A pen sketch, a floor plan or 3 reference images in. A 3D house that builds itself out.
A Claude Code skill. Every board, every tatami mat, every shoji strip and every frame is code, rendered in Blender.

3 houses inside  ·  2,444 parts in the courtyard house alone  ·  no 3D files of the houses  ·  CC0 materials

What it makes

You hand Claude what you have: a sketch on paper, a plan from a sales brochure, or a few images of the look you want. Claude reads it into numbers (walls, rooms, openings, the scale), writes the whole house as one Blender script with every part a separate object, renders stills next to your references and fixes what differs. Then it films the house building itself on top of the input, brings it to life and walks inside, with a sound on every part that lands.


Courtyard house · from a pen sketch
14 x 14 m, a red maple in a 7 x 7 m court. The frame, the floors, the walls, the shoji and the roof land on the paper in white clay, each system in its own colour, with a counter.
Cliff villa · from 4 references
A travertine pavilion on a headland, an infinity pool over the cliff. Tiles and blocks fly in, the pool fills, the lights come on, a dive in through the glass.
Apartment · from a brochure plan
Walls traced from the plan at its scale bar, doors and furniture read on a metre grid. A dollhouse, then a walk through the rooms.

How it works
Numbers first The input becomes rooms, walls, openings and furniture in metres before any geometry. A sketch's dimension labels beat its pixels.
Built like a carpenter Footings, sills, posts, beams, rafters, roof panels, cladding, boards, tatami, kumiko: each its own object, tagged with its stage.
Stills against references Render low, put the reference beside it, list the differences, fix, render again.
The film opens on the input The sketch is the first frame. The camera spirals down out of it while the parts land on the paper.
Fits an 8 GB card Bevels baked before motion blur, scanned conifers decimated 8x.

Install

npx skills add Nyxera0x/blueprint -g -a claude-code

You also need Blender 4.2+, Python 3 with pillow (plus opencv-python and numpy to read a plan image), and ffmpeg. Fetch the CC0 materials once per house:

python ~/.claude/skills/blueprint/houses/courtyard/fetch_assets.py

Then open Claude Code and type /blueprint with your sketch, your plan or your references.

Run an example yourself

blender -b --factory-startup -P houses/courtyard/build.py -- tatami engawa --samples 192 --res 1920x1080
blender -b --factory-startup -P houses/courtyard/film.py -- --res 1920x1080 --samples 64

Stills and frames land in blueprint-out/. See SKILL.md for the film's sound, the counter overlay and the method for a new house.

Credits

Materials, plants and rocks: Poly Haven, CC0. The sound kit renders everything in code; its few recorded samples are listed with their CC0 sources in sfx/samples/SOURCES.md. Code: MIT.
